MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Centre

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date] 2004
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Fragile X syndrome

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Pediatric patient referred for molecular genetic testing to investigate possible Fragile X syndrome. Additional testing for Angelman syndrome has been requested.

METHODOLOGY
PCR-based assay for CGG repeat expansion analysis in the FMR1 gene (FRAXA) and GCC repeat expansion analysis in the FMR2 gene (FRAXE). DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leucocytes. PCR amplification was performed using fluorescently labeled primers flanking the repeat regions. Fragment analysis was performed by capillary electrophoresis with accurate sizing of PCR products to determine repeat numbers.

RESULTS

FMR1 Gene (FRAXA) Analysis:
Allele 1: 29 CGG repeats
Allele 2: 31 CGG repeats
Result: NORMAL heterozygous female pattern

FMR2 Gene (FRAXE) Analysis:
Allele 1: 12 GCC repeats
Allele 2: 16 GCC repeats
Result: NORMAL heterozygous female pattern

Reference Ranges:
FRAXA (FMR1): Normal: 6-50 CGG repeats
FRAXE (FMR2): Normal: 6-30 GCC repeats

INTERPRETATION
This patient shows normal heterozygous results for both FRAXA and FRAXE testing. Both alleles for FMR1 fall within the normal range (6-50 repeats), and both alleles for FMR2 fall within the normal range (6-30 repeats). These results reduce the likelihood of Fragile X syndrome or carrier status to less than 1%.

TEST LIMITATIONS
This PCR-based assay detects CGG repeat expansions in FMR1 and GCC repeat expansions in FMR2. A small percentage of Fragile X cases may result from point mutations or rearrangements within the FMR1 gene that would not be detected by this method. If clinical suspicion remains high, additional testing methods may be considered.

SUMMARY AND RECOMMENDATIONS
Molecular testing for Fragile X syndrome (FRAXA and FRAXE) shows normal results. The sample has been forwarded for Angelman syndrome testing as requested. A follow-up report will be issued when this testing is complete.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
